name: Starter: Lithuanian
about: Lithuanian cases and word order in real, everyday sentences.

words.aš: I (man: to me; manęs: me; mano: my)
words.sektis: to go (well) (kaip sekasi: how's it going)
words.tu: you, to one person, informally (tau: to you; tavo: your)
words.būti: to be (yra: is, there is; nėra: isn't, there's no)
words.turėti: to have; to have to (turiu eiti: I have to go)
words.eiti: to go, usually on foot; to leave (Dabar turiu eiti: I have to go)
words.važiuoti: to go (by car, bus or train)
words.koks: what, what kind of (masculine; feminine kokia)
words.patikti: to please (man patinka: I like it)
words.grįžti: to come back, to get back
words.taksi: taxi (it never changes; važiuoti taksi: to go by taxi)
words.pas: to or at someone's (pas močiutę: to grandma's)
words.kinas: movie theater (į kiną: to the movies)
words.veikti: to do, to be up to (ką veiki: what are you up to)
words.pranešti: to let someone know, to tell

noreciau.about: A polite way to order or ask for something, with the genitive after it: Norėčiau kavos (I'd like a coffee).

atsiprasau.about: To get someone's attention or say sorry, to anyone.

items.text: Vieną arbatą ir vieną vandenį, prašau.
items.means: A tea and a water, please.
wrong: Vieną arbata ir vieną vandenį, prašau.
Vieną arbatą ir vienas vandenį, prašau.

items.means: I have a brother and a sister.
Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
Excuse me, how much is it?
I live in a small house.
My mother goes to the city.
Tomorrow I'm going to the city.

items.text: Turiu vieną seserį ir du brolius.
items.means: I have one sister and two brothers.
wrong: Turiu viena sesuo ir du brolius.
Turiu vieną seserį ir du broliai.

items.means: I don't know where he lives.
My mom works at a hospital.
I live in a small apartment.
There's a book on the table.
There's no milk in the fridge.

items.text: Turime didelę virtuvę ir mažą balkoną.
items.means: We have a big kitchen and a small balcony.
wrong: Turime didelį virtuvę ir mažą balkoną.
Turime didelė virtuvė ir mažas balkonas.

items.means: When I get home, I'll make dinner.
Can I get a glass of water?
I want to eat something sweet.
I like cooking with my mom.
I'd like a coffee with milk.
I'm going to the store for bread.
Tomorrow I'll go to work by bus.
The train was ten minutes late.
Grandma's waiting for us at the station.
On Saturday we're going to grandma's.

items.text: Ar eisi su mumis į kiną?
items.means: Are you coming to the movies with us?
wrong: Ar eisi su mes į kiną?

items.means: We're going to the beach this weekend.
I've been learning Lithuanian for a year.
What are you doing this weekend?

items.text: Tikiuosi, kad rytoj bus gražus oras.
items.means: I hope the weather's nice tomorrow.
wrong: Tikiuosi, kad rytoj bus graži oras.

concept.line: The verb's ending marks the person: (aš) gyvenu, (tu) gyveni, (jis, ji) gyvena, (mes) gyvename, (jūs) gyvenate, (jie) gyvena.
A yes/no question usually starts with ar (Ar kalbi angliškai?); otherwise a question word like kur, ką or koks usually starts the question; Lithuanian adds no do.

words.means: esu = I am; esi = you are; nesu = I am not

concept.line: Lithuanian has no words for a, an or the; context does their work: Esu mokytojas; Ant stalo yra knyga.

words.means: turiu = I have; turi = you have; neturiu = I do not have

concept.line: The genitive means of (tėčio mašina: Dad's car; stiklinė vandens), says some of or what you want (Norėčiau kavos; ką nors saldaus: something sweet), follows be and ant (be cukraus, ant stalo), is the object of verbs like laukti, norėti and mokytis (Stotyje mūsų laukia močiutė), and says what you go for: Einu į parduotuvę duonos.

words.means: kalbi = you speak; kalbu = I speak
nesuprantu = I do not understand; supranti = you understand

concept.line: A Lithuanian verb marks the person, so aš (I), tu (you) and mes (we) are usually left out: Gyvenu mažame bute (I live in a small apartment).

words.means: name = in a house; namas = house
mažas = small; mažame = in a small
gyvenu = I live; gyveni = you live; gyvena = lives
eini = you are going; einu = I go

concept.line: The accusative marks the direct object (Geriu kavą), follows į and pas for where you're going (į parduotuvę, į kiną, pas močiutę), and says when or for how long: šeštadienį, savaitgalį, metus.

words.means: dirbu = I work; dirbti = to work
